extracted.intended_audience: researchers, librarians, journal editors, and scholars interested in open access publishing and overlay journals
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical study identifying currently active overlay journals and examining their characteristics (publication model, fields, publishers, fees, and bibliometric standing) using web searches and contacts with service providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlay journal publication model (open access repositories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlay journals are characterised by their articles being published on open access repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often the article starts in its initial preprint form on a repository; this repository-based publication is a defining feature of the overlay model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint-as-prerequisite for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles often already start in their initial preprint form as a prerequisite for submission to the journal prior to initiating the peer-review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model commonly requires that manuscripts exist as repository preprints before the overlay journal begins peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical subject coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Most overlay journals publish articles in natural sciences, mathematics or computer sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current landscape is concentrated in these disciplines rather than being evenly distributed across all fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher type (academic groups vs formal organisations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlay journals are commonly published by groups of academics rather than formal organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many overlay journals are grassroots or scholar-led initiatives instead of being run by large commercial or society publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author fee policy
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the investigated journals required fees from authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of author fees is likely related to cost-effective aspects of the overlay publishing model; fee policies are a salient characteristic when assessing overlay journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliometric standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Overlay journals may also rank highly within the traditional journal citation metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite their different model, some overlay journals achieve high standing on established citation metrics — this is relevant when evaluating perceived quality or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current prevalence compared to OA journals
rubrics_metrics.description: The current presence of overlay journals remains diminutive compared to the overall number of open access journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While new overlay journals have been established recently, their absolute numbers are small relative to the broader OA journal ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determinants of future growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the growth in adoption of open access preprint repositories and researchers' willingness to publish in overlay journals will determine the model's wider impact on scholarly publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption factors (repository uptake, community acceptance) are key criteria when projecting the sustainability and expansion of overlay journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification methodology for active overlay journals
rubrics_metrics.description: The study utilised an explorative web search and contacted key service providers for additional information; final sample consisted of 34 overlay journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling a set of active overlay journals, combine systematic web searches with outreach to service providers and confirm candidate journals against defining characteristics (repository publication, preprint prerequisite, publisher type, fee policy).
